predictive_observations: The pool was seeded directly on PumpSwap and never went through the pump.fun curve (migrated_unix=0, blank launchpad, mint not ending in 'pump'). lp_burn_ratio was 0 and RugCheck showed 0% LP locked plus a 'Large Amount of LP Unlocked' danger flag. Whoever held the LP could remove it at any time, and liquidity went to $0 inside the first hour after entry.
Liquidity (~$44.9k) was about equal to market cap (~$44.2k). That fits a pool the deployer seeded and still owns, not a curve that graduated with liquidity burned.
creator_token_status='creator_close' with creator_balance=0, next to an unlocked LP. The creator had nothing left to lose in the token and still controlled the LP.
The creator's history was empty (creator_launched_token_count=0). creator_best_token_ath_mcap (~$51.4k) matches this token's own ATH, so the history said nothing reassuring.
The report's structural call (market_feasibility 'poor', p_rug 70, 'fade') rested on the LP-control facts above. The outcome matched: liquidity collapsed and the recorded net return was -100%.
misleading_observations: 1,189 unique buyers in the first hour looked like broad retail participation. Buyer counts say nothing about whether the LP owner will pull liquidity, and they had no bearing on this outcome.

'This pair won the copycat race' (most liquidity of the same-name copies) was used as a point in its favor. The pair had the most liquidity because it was the one whose LP had not been pulled yet. That made it the biggest remaining target, not the canonical token.

The narrative work (the meme template, the QuantKeef tweet, the 'spreading' stage) took much of the research effort. Nothing in it could have told us whether the LP would be pulled, so it had no effect on the result.
Contract security looked clean (mint and freeze authority renounced, 0% tax). That is irrelevant to an LP-removal rug and could have made the token look safer than it was.

Price-path metrics after the fact mislead too. MFE was +33%, MAE only -8%, no -20% level was touched, and the time-exit gross return was +32%. Price stayed where it was while liquidity went to 0, which is the signature of an LP pull. A price-only reading would score this as a mild winner. Also, min_liquidity_24h (42,004) contradicts exit_liquidity 0 and liquidity_collapse=true. The outcome record has an internal inconsistency that should be audited.
evidence_that_should_have_changed_conclu: The conclusion was already 'fade/rug', so no evidence called for reversing it. But the p_rug of 70 was probably too low given what was in the packet.

The same-name siblings are a live record of rugs in this exact launch wave. ApdL… still showed $236.9k of hourly volume with only $10.26 of liquidity. 8HjG… showed $167k hourly volume with $3 of liquidity, and E3NQ… $131k with $1.48. 56P2… and CHEk… had roughly $0 liquidity. Tokens that traded heavily and now have near-zero liquidity have almost certainly had their LP removed. Several copies had been rugged within about 40 minutes. The report called them 'mostly dead' and 'splitting attention' but did not treat them as a base rate for how pools in this burst end. That should have pushed p_rug toward 85-90% and firmed up the no-trade call.
Between T2 and entry, market cap had already fallen from ~$44k to ~$31k and liquidity from ~$44.9k to ~$39.2k. Liquidity was already draining before the report's decision was acted on.

hypotheses_proposed.statement: Pools seeded directly on PumpSwap, where (a) migrated_unix=0 and there is no launchpad, (b) lp_burn_ratio=0 and 0% of LP is locked, (c) liquidity/market-cap ratio is at least 0.8, and (d) the creator holds 0% or creator_status is 'close', will see liquidity fall by 90% or more within 6h of decision at a clearly higher rate than pump.fun-graduated pools of similar market cap and age.
hypotheses_proposed.conditions: Solana PumpSwap pairs under 2h old and under $300k market cap, with all four conditions visible at T2. Compare against graduated pump.fun pools (LP burned) matched on age and market cap.
hypotheses_proposed.market_structure_rationale: When the deployer seeds the pool and keeps the LP tokens, one transaction can remove all the SOL. With a 0% creator token balance, the deployer's only remaining stake is the LP, so pulling it is their dominant exit. Graduated pump.fun pools burn their LP, which removes that option.

hypotheses_proposed.statement: When same-name or same-ticker tokens launched within the previous 60 minutes include at least 3 with liquidity under $100 and hourly volume over $10k (i.e., already drained), the surviving highest-liquidity copy will have its liquidity collapse within 6h at a higher rate than comparable tokens with no drained siblings.
hypotheses_proposed.conditions: Applies when the same_ticker_or_name_tokens list at T2 shows a burst of copies created within about 1h of the target, and the target's LP is unlocked. Does not apply when the target's LP is burned or locked.
hypotheses_proposed.market_structure_rationale: Copycat bursts are often run by the same deployer farm or by operators using the same playbook: seed the pool, pull in volume, remove the LP. Siblings with near-zero liquidity despite recent heavy volume show that playbook is running in this wave. The copy with the most liquidity is often just the one that has not been pulled yet.

hypotheses_proposed.statement: For bracket or return scoring, an exit where liquidity is 0 and price is unchanged should be treated as a total loss, with a separate 'LP-pull' label. Price-barrier metrics (MFE, level touches) will systematically overstate performance on these cases.
hypotheses_proposed.conditions: Any candidate where exit_liquidity is 0 or liquidity_collapse is true while the price series shows no matching drop.
hypotheses_proposed.market_structure_rationale: Removing LP takes the reserves out without a swap, so the last traded price stays where it was even though nothing can be sold at it.

structured_output.summary: The report's call (fade, p_rug 70, p_runner 11) matched the outcome: liquidity went from ~$39k at entry to $0 within the first hour, and the recorded net return was -100%. Its correct reasoning was structural. The pool was seeded by the deployer directly on PumpSwap with 0% LP locked or burned, liquidity was about equal to market cap, and the creator held 0% with status 'creator_close'. Together, those made an LP pull the dominant exit, and the report identified them. The narrative and tweet research, the unique-buyer count, clean contract security and 'won the copycat race' had no bearing on the result. The report under-used one piece of evidence: several same-name siblings from the same ~40-minute burst already showed heavy hourly volume on liquidity of $0-10. That is a direct record of LP pulls in this wave and should have pushed p_rug toward 85-90%. The outcome was only partially knowable. It was rug-prone in a way the packet made clear, but whether the pull would land in the first hour could not be known. Price-only metrics (+33% MFE, no -20% touch) would wrongly score this as a small winner, because an LP pull leaves the price unchanged. The outcome record also contradicts itself (min_liquidity_24h of 42k vs. exit liquidity of 0) and should be audited. One case cannot confirm the method. The hypotheses above are stated so they can be tested on future candidates using only information available at decision time.
